Bodegas Aalto.region: Quintanilla de Arriba, Ribera del Duero

Gaia Wines.about: Gaia was founded in 1994 by two agronomists, Yiannis Paraskevopoulos and Leon Karatsalos, with wineries in Nemea on the Peloponnese and on Santorini. Their first release was just 9,800 bottles of Thalassitis, a Santorini Assyrtiko that helped put the grape on the world map. The Santorini winery sits on the beach near Kamari, in a stone building where sun-dried tomatoes were processed a century ago. To test how Assyrtiko ages, they sank bottles of Thalassitis about 20 metres under the sea off the island and compared them with the same wine kept in the cellar. Gaia is now one of the names most associated with the revival of serious Greek wine.

wines.Ammonite Assyrtiko: Ammonite is Gaia's top Santorini white, a single-vineyard Assyrtiko from a plot called Thalassina at the highest point of Megalochori, around 200 metres above the sea. The vines are ungrafted and are said to have root systems more than three centuries old, because the phylloxera louse that wiped out Europe's vines never took hold in Santorini's volcanic soil. Rather than growing up posts, the vines are woven into low baskets called kouloura that sit on the ground, so the grapes hang inside, sheltered from the island's fierce winds. The wine spends 15 months on its lees, with a small portion in new French oak, and is named after Gaia's emblem, the fossilised sea creature called an ammonite.

Krug.about: Krug was founded in Reims in 1843 by Joseph Krug, a German-born winemaker from Mainz who had learned his trade at the Champagne house Jacquesson. His idea was radical for the time: to make the finest champagne every single year, whatever the weather, by blending wines from many plots and many vintages instead of relying on one good harvest. In 1848 he set out these principles in a notebook addressed to his six-year-old son, Paul, and the house still treats it as its founding text. Krug takes the comparison with music literally: through a project called Krug Echoes, it has commissioned composers to write pieces expressing how they perceive the taste of particular cuvées. Now part of LVMH, the house is still regarded as the benchmark for prestige champagne.

wines.Grande Cuvée 174ème Édition: Grande Cuvée is Krug's signature champagne, and the edition number counts how many times the blend has been recreated since Joseph Krug's first. The 174ème Édition is built around the 2018 harvest, but it combines 143 separate wines from ten different years, the oldest dating back to 2001. Reserve wines from the house's library make up 36% of the blend, which is 54% Pinot Noir, 29% Chardonnay and 17% Meunier. Every bottle carries a six-digit Krug iD on its back label, which you can look up online to read that bottle's own story, including its blend, when it was disgorged and suggestions for food and music to go with it.

Vega Sicilia.region: Valbuena de Duero, Ribera del Duero
Vega Sicilia.about: Founded in 1864 in Valbuena de Duero, Vega Sicilia is Spain's most celebrated estate and the reason Ribera del Duero is famous at all. Its founder, Eloy Lecanda, planted Bordeaux varieties from France alongside the local Tinto Fino (Tempranillo), giving the wines a structure that set them apart. Despite the name, it has nothing to do with Sicily: the land was known as the "Pago de la Vega Santa Cecilia," the meadow of Saint Cecilia, and the saint's name was worn down over time into "Sicilia." The estate is known for very long ageing before release, and it was famous for over a century before the region won official appellation status in 1982. Owned by the Álvarez family since 1982, it remains a benchmark for age-worthy Spanish red.

wines.Unico: Unico is Vega Sicilia's flagship and one of the world's most sought-after reds, made mainly from Tinto Fino with a share of Cabernet Sauvignon. It is made only in years the estate judges worthy, and is skipped altogether in lesser vintages. It is typically released around a decade after the harvest, after years in barrels of different sizes and then a long rest in bottle, so a new release is usually already older than most wines ever get before they're opened. The result is a wine built to evolve for decades more in the cellar.
wines.Valbuena 5°: Valbuena is the estate's second red, from younger vines and a different blend that includes Merlot alongside Tinto Fino. The "5°" is a label you can read literally: it stands for quinto año, the fifth year, because the wine is released five years after harvest. It sees less time in barrel than Unico and is approachable much earlier, but it still ages gracefully. Many regard it as the best way into the Vega Sicilia style without the Unico price.
